transcript: My friend Sylvia and I couldn't get tickets to the Super Bowl, so we went to see The Notebook on Broadway instead. It was good, but it didn't quite live up to the hype for me. I don't wanna sound like a hater because it really is quite good so let's start with the positives. It is beautifully staged, directed, and designed. The lighting design in particular is stunning and so creatively done. The performances are amazing, the vocals are absolutely top tier. And the book is good too — it actually isn't cringey which I think is pretty impressive for a cliche love story. Getting into the lukewarm territory for me is the music, which is very good and super well orchestrated, but the only thing was that nothing was super anthemic. I was kind of hoping for a big She Used To Be Mine kind of song but I think the closest we get is a song called My Days beautifully performed by Joy Woods in Act II. The score just overall doesn't have quite as much oomph as I was hoping for, it's good but it's a little safe I think. Nothing is bad about it, but I wondered if it could have gone further if that makes sense. My only other minor critique is that I wanted the show to hit harder emotionally. Some tears were definitely shed, and I could hear the audible sniffles around me in the last 15 minutes or so of the show, but I kind of wanted to be destroyed. I can't really say how it compares to the book or the movie, because I'm not familiar with either of them but this musical is great overall. If you like Ingrid Michaelson music, if you like big Broadway designs, if you like to cry, or even if you just like great singing, you will definitely find something to enjoy here.With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer gives a clear recommendation despite some reservations, praising the staging, performances, and vocals while noting the music is 'safe' and wishing for more emotional impact. The conclusion strongly recommends it for multiple audience types.
